name: Daniel
label: Hand-built playlists, distrusts recommendations
who: I have been a Premium member for over ten years and listen for many hours a day, at home, at work, in the car and on my PS5. I build most of my own playlists by hand and rarely let Spotify's recommendations drive what I hear.
value_for_money: Calls himself a Premium customer who has paid for over ten years, but does not discuss price itself. As a professional musician he says a subscription is almost necessary for transcribing other people's songs, so the value he describes is library access rather than cost.
loyalty: The years of curated playlists and liked songs keep him here [7][11]. Discover Weekly repeats and weak recommendations are parts he works around rather than relies on [10][29]. He says he cannot go back to Apple Music [33], and the evidence does not name anything else that would make him leave.
pain_points: Discover Weekly and playlists recycle the same top-40 songs
Made For You playlists crowd out the listening experience and cannot be turned off
No folders or archiving for playlists
likes: Song radio and mixes that stay on-point
Liked Songs as a long-term library
Release Radar and Discover Weekly as occasional sources
Crossfade and the ability to block artists
reasons_to_stay: He values his large library, playlists and liked songs, and says he loves Spotify and uses it all day for music, podcasts and audiobooks [8][11][12]. The app performs well on his phone most of the time, and years of playlists are built there, so he keeps using it while complaining about recommendations [0][5].
tone: Thoughtful, opinionated and long-form, often pairing praise with specific complaints.
